email.body1:
Mike, saw Teamworks raised $235M and acquired PFF enterprise, Opteamal, and Telemetry.

Growth and acquisitions at that pace usually mean more in-market accounts in play than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Teamworks off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Mike, quick follow-up for Teamworks.

Post-raise and mid-acquisition spree, board expectations on pipeline tend to jump faster than headcount can. Most BD leaders don't actually know how many booked meetings it takes to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and recovering the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Teamworks needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Mike, last bit of proof for Teamworks.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Teamworks's reply rate likely compares to other growth-stage SaaS teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Mike, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Right after a raise and several acquisitions, I know the GTM stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your BD motion? I'll tailor it to Teamworks either way.
